meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas (live data, not an archived version; give corpus_snapshot and source_commit). doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Freed ULK1 nucleates the autophagosome - the self-eating programme that recycles damaged parts and is the leading candidate mechanism for mTOR inhibition's benefits.
data.mechanism_beginner: Freed ULK1 kicks off autophagy – the cell's recycling programme, and the leading idea for why blocking this pathway might be beneficial.
data.context: LC3-II accumulation, the standard readout for this step, marks autophagosome number, not flux: it rises whether autophagosomes are being made faster or degraded slower (e.g. under lysosomal/fusion block), so it cannot alone distinguish increased autophagy from stalled autophagy. A flux assay (e.g. LC3-II with and without a degradation blocker, or p62 turnover) is needed to tell the two apart.
data.boundary: Mammalian cell studies (GAN2009, HOS2009, EGA2010). Autophagosome initiation is shown in cultured cells. Whether autophagy carries the benefits of mTOR inhibition in whole animals is not tested by these sources.
